paragraph: Westwood's single-family market is where nearly all the action is, with 20 sales over six months at a median of $794,500 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.11. Ninety percent of those homes sold above asking and the median time to contract was 10 days. That is a real seller's market, and buyers should expect multiple offer situations on anything well presented. Sales ran from $435,000 to $1,525,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Condos and townhouses are a much smaller slice at 5 sales and a median of $381,000, moving in 12 days at a ratio slightly above list. Five closings is too thin to call a trend, but the pattern matches the houses: quick, at or above ask. On seasonality, the monthly counts are small enough that no single month proves much, though June and July both closed 5 single-family sales at medians of $799,000 and $875,000, which is strength holding into midsummer rather than the usual drift. If this town follows the normal arc, expect fall closings to come in softer. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat, since both are competitive. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle and lower price point of a condo.
